summary: Shunpaku Nakao specialized in Buddhist studies. He served at Shuchiin University, holding the posts of assistant professor as attested in 1963 and professor as attested in 1976.

Shunryu Suzuki (1904-1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Eihei-ji, and under several teachers. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe (1939-2021) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1958-1962), taught at Hosen Gakuen College (~2004-2010), and was a professor at Shikoku University as attested in 2015.
Shunsho Terakawa (1928-2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950-1953). He served as an emeritus professor at Otani University (~1963-2000).
Shuntaro Kondo (born 1974) is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011 and served there as a part-time lecturer as attested in 2012.

Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930-2014) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, including under Naoshiro Tsuji, and later taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1970-2001).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993, he served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927-2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, where he earned a doctorate in 1962 and later served as an assistant professor (~1968-1992).
Shuyu Sakurai (born 1916) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1940-1943) and served as an emeritus professor at Komazawa University (~1950-1994).

Shwe Zan Aung (1871-1932) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. at the University of Rangoon in 1891 and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912-1985) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University, graduating by 1936, and later served there as a professor from around 1956 to 1982.

Shōren Ihara (1923-1999) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyushu University, including assistant professor (attested 1959-1965), and was a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996-1998).

Shōyū Hanayama (1931-1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950-1957). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1968-1995) and chairperson of the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1995.
Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014), following studies with multiple traditional teachers.

Sibani Das Gupta is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate degree at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibaraj Chetry specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was supervised for his doctorate by Sibnath Sarma, studied under several other teachers, and served as a Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College as attested in 2012.

Sibnath Sarma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir and served as Professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999-2012).

Sicheng Liang (1901-1972) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915-1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924-1927), later holding a post at Peking University.

Sidney Lee (1859-1926) was an academic who studied at the City of London School (~1872-1878) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878-1882). He later held a post at Queen Mary University of London from around 1913 to 1924.

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844-1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (PhD 1867) under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, becoming an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.
